--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. # OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review. Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests. ## Wiki index - [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md) - [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md) - [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md) - [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md) - [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md) - [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md) ## Main project file The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml). Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'

const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8
const readText = (directory, name) => { try { return readFileSync(join(directory, name), 'utf8').trim() } catch { return '' } }
const readJson = (directory, name) => { try { return JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(directory, name), 'utf8')) } catch { return null } }

// Optional admin stats for /run posts: WARP outcome, current and final model,
// per-attempt results and elapsed time. Missing files simply omit fields.
export function buildStats(directory, now = Date.now()) {
  if (!directory) return {}
  const stats = {}
  const warp = readJson(directory, 'warp-status.json')
  if (warp && typeof warp === 'object') {
    stats.warp = { decision: warp.decision, result: warp.result }
    for (const key of ['attempt', 'egress_prefix', 'egress_prefix64', 'colo', 'warp_result', 'proxy', 'switched_at', 'proxy_drop']) if (warp[key] !== undefined && warp[key] !== '') stats.warp[key] = warp[key]
    // DataImpulse relay byte counts (numbers only) for cost tracking.
    const bytes = readJson(directory, 'proxy-bytes.json')
    if (bytes && Number.isSafeInteger(bytes.up) && Number.isSafeInteger(bytes.down)) stats.warp.proxy_bytes = bytes.up + bytes.down
  }
  const model = readText(directory, 'main-model')
  if (model) stats.model = model
  // Pinned runner commit for this build, so the project page can show which runtime ran it.
  const runtime = readText(directory, 'runtime-ref.txt')
  if (/^[a-f0-9]{40}$/i.test(runtime)) stats.runtime = runtime.toLowerCase()
  const attempts = readJson(directory, 'model-attempts.json')
  if (Array.isArray(attempts) && attempts.length) {
    stats.attempts = attempts.slice(-MAX_ATTEMPTS).map(({ model, outcome, code, error_class, duration_ms }) => ({ model, outcome, code, ...(error_class ? { error_class } : {}), duration_ms }))
    const done = attempts.findLast(attempt => attempt?.code === 0)
    if (done?.model) stats.final_model = done.model
    // OpenCode's own working time: wall time of each `opencode run` attempt (spawn to exit + terminal check).
    // Unlike duration_ms it excludes runner setup and the post-build access hold (up to 5 h on success).
    const work = attempts.map(attempt => Number(attempt?.duration_ms)).filter(ms => Number.isFinite(ms) && ms >= 0)
    if (work.length) stats.opencode_ms = Math.round(work.reduce((sum, ms) => sum + ms, 0))

# Device Relay Protocol v1 (omsite ↔ Android)

Blind HTTPS CONNECT through the owner's phone. Phone never sees keys or prompts.
When the phone WebSocket drops, the run falls back to normal egress (WARP / DataImpulse / runner).

## Roles
- **phone**: Android app, WebSocket client, while on-screen only (no foreground service).
- **runner**: GitHub Actions job, opens a second WebSocket; local `127.0.0.1` CONNECT relay feeds OpenCode.
- **a2 (omsite)**: authenticates both sides, pairs by GitHub login, bridges streams, enforces allowlist.

## Endpoints (same-origin per brand host)
| Method | Path | Who | Auth |
|--------|------|-----|------|
| `POST` | `/api/device-relay/token` | phone | session cookie `omgithub_session` (SameSite=Lax) |
| `GET`  | `/api/device-relay/status` | phone | session cookie |
| `POST` | `/api/device-relay/revoke` | phone | session cookie |
| `POST` | `/api/github/:owner/:repo/issues/:n/device-relay` | runner | GitHub Actions OIDC Bearer (same as `/ci-proxy`) |
| `GET`  | `/api/github/:owner/:repo/issues/:n/device-relay` | runner | OIDC; fast probe `{available:bool}` |
| `WSS`  | `/api/device-relay/ws` | phone + runner | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (not cookie) |

Hosts: `omgithub.com`, `android-create.<family>` (incl. `lolgames.net`). No shared sign-in across families.

## Tokens
**Device token** (`POST /token`):
```json
{ "token": "<opaque>", "expires_in": 600, "ws_url": "wss://<host>/api/device-relay/ws", "protocol": 1 }
```
- Bound to `user.id` + `user.login` (lowercased). TTL 10 min; refresh while app open (re-POST).
- Guests rejected (401). Any signed-in user allowed.
- Opaque HMAC like `omg1.` callback tokens (reuse `sessionSecret`); not a JWT with secrets inside.

**Run token** (`POST .../device-relay`):
```json
{ "token": "<opaque>", "expires_in": 3600, "ws_url": "wss://<host>/api/device-relay/ws",
  "available": true, "protocol": 1, "max_streams": 8, "max_bytes": 157286400 }
```
- Same OIDC checks as `ci-proxy.mjs`: PlayGround only, active `issueRuns` record, trusted workflow.
- Bound to `owner/repo#number` + `run` + `attempt` + owner login (`owner` path = GitHub login).
- `available:false` (200) when no phone online for that login → runner skips without error.
- 409 if run not active; 403 if issue owner ≠ phone owner mapping.

## WebSocket framing
First message after connect MUST be text JSON `hello`. Then mixed text (control) + binary (payload).

### Binary data frame
```
offset 0  u32be stream_id
offset 4  payload bytes (TLS ciphertext; never logged)
```
Max frame payload: 64 KiB. Larger writes are split across frames.

### Control messages (text JSON)
```json
{"v":1,"type":"hello","role":"device"|"runner","token":"<same bearer>"}
{"v":1,"type":"ready","user":"<login>","max_streams":8}
{"v":1,"type":"open","id":1,"host":"opencode.ai","port":443}
{"v":1,"type":"opened","id":1}
{"v":1,"type":"open_error","id":1,"code":"forbidden"|"refused"|"timeout"|"offline","message":"..."}
{"v":1,"type":"close","id":1,"reason":"eof"|"error"|"revoke"|"cap"}
{"v":1,"type":"device_offline","code":"eof"|"revoke"}
{"v":1,"type":"ping","t":<unix_ms>}
{"v":1,"type":"pong","t":<unix_ms>}
{"v":1,"type":"window","id":1,"credit":32}
{"v":1,"type":"error","code":"unauthorized"|"version"|"busy","message":"..."}
```

### Stream lifecycle (runner → a2 → phone)
1. Runner local relay gets OpenCode `CONNECT host:443`.
2. Runner sends `open {id,host,port}`; a2 validates allowlist; forwards to phone.
3. Phone TCP-connects `host:443` (OS stack = phone public IP); replies `opened` or `open_error`.
4. a2 tells runner `opened` → local relay answers `HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established`.
5. Bidirectional binary frames until `close` or WS drop.
6. On phone WS drop: a2 sends `device_offline` to the runner, `open_error/offline` for pending opens, and `close` for live streams. The runner records `last_error=offline`, fails every tunnel, and the watcher calls `drop-proxy.sh` within ~2 s — even when no request is in flight.

### Heartbeat
- Either side sends `ping` every 15s; expect `pong` within 10s.
- Missed pong → close WS. Phone reconnects with a fresh/refreshed token.
- a2 idle-kills a device WS after 45s without ping/pong or traffic.

### Flow control
- Per-stream credit window: start 32 frames; each `window` adds credit; sender stops at 0.
- Max concurrent streams per pair: **8** (`max_streams`).
- Global per-user: 1 device WS, 1 runner WS per active run.

### Versioning
- `hello.v` / `protocol` field. Unknown major → `error code=version` and close.
- Additive fields OK; removing/renaming needs v2.

## Host allowlist (port 443 only)
Enforced on **a2** (before `open` reaches phone) and **phone** (defense in depth). Reject anything else.

Exact hosts (no wildcards in v1):
```
opencode.ai
openrouter.ai
```
`models.opencode.ai` is **not** on the phone — runner egress mux sends it to WARP / DataImpulse / direct (same as pre-device).

Deny: `models.opencode.ai` (on the device path), `github.com`, `*.github.com`, `githubcopilot.com`, `githubusercontent.com`, private/literal IPs, non-443.

## Runner integration
1. Probe `GET .../device-relay` (OIDC). If `available`, fetch run token via `POST`.
2. Start local relay (sibling of `proxy-relay.mjs`) listening `127.0.0.1`; upstream = device WSS.
3. Creds file pattern: write once, delete after read; never put token in OpenCode env.
4. `start-opencode-serve.sh` gets `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` only (the egress mux when the phone is up); keep existing `NO_PROXY` for GitHub/Copilot.
5. Priority when device presence on: **mux(device for allowlist, WARP/DataImpulse/direct for `models.opencode.ai`) → else WARP → DataImpulse → bare**.
6. Mid-run phone loss: relay `onFailure` → `drop-proxy.sh` (reuse `opencode-proxy.fallback`).
7. Byte cap: 150 MB default (same as `PROXY_RELAY_MAX_BYTES`); totals + per-host counts; no payloads logged.

## Limits & abuse
- Device token rate: 30/hour/user. Run token: 1 active per issue run.
- Cap 150 MB/run; concurrent streams 8; connect timeout 15s; idle stream 120s.
- Logs: stream id, host, bytes, durations, error codes — **never** Authorization, cookies, TLS bytes, prompts.
- `POST /revoke` (or Settings clear): drop device WS, invalidate outstanding device tokens, in-flight streams `close reason=revoke`.
- Pairing: phone `user.login` must equal issue `owner` (PlayGround under that login). View-as admin sessions are allowed (Igor, 2026-11-05).

## Android client checklist
- Debug setting on → obtain token → open WSS while Activity resumed; close on `onPause`/`onStop`.
- No new permissions; no foreground service; no key/prompt access (blind TCP only).
- WebView session cookie already set via Custom Tab redeem; `POST /token` is same-origin XHR/fetch with credentials.
- Implement allowlist identically; reject `open` locally if mismatch.
- Reconnect with backoff (1s, 2s, 5s, max 15s) while setting on and Activity resumed.

## Mock phone (for omsite / desktop proof)
- **omsite** `scripts/mock-device-relay-client.mjs`: needs `ws` + `server/lib/device-relay.mjs`; used by unit tests.
- **OhMyGithub** `scripts/mock-device-relay-client.mjs` (preferred on a Mac): Node built-ins only; same protocol. Docs: `scripts/DEVICE-RELAY-DESKTOP.md`.
Both connect with a device token, accept `open` only for allowlisted hosts, and pipe to real TCP (or a loopback echo under `MOCK_ECHO=1`). Point at live `wss://omgithub.com/api/device-relay/ws` (or brand host). Opens still require a paired runner.

## Decisions (Igor, 2026-11-05)
1. Priority: phone first, then WARP (device → WARP → DataImpulse → bare).
2. Allowlist was three hosts; **2026-11-05 (scope change):** `models.opencode.ai` removed — only `opencode.ai` + `openrouter.ai` use the phone; models stay on WARP/DataImpulse/runner via egress mux.
3. Copilot/Fusion never through the phone (NO_PROXY).
4. Live WS presence is enough; no server-side "enabled" flag.
5. Admins viewing as another user are not blocked.
6. Per-run cap stays 150 MB.
